title: Defend Grocery Channel Share with Joint Business Plans in Top 3 Grocery Customers
description: Create 3–4 joint business plans (JBPs) with Dunnes, Musgrave, and Tesco in the Grocery channel focused on volume-driving mechanics (feature & display, secondary siting, meal deals, and cross-category bundles) in the core Food and Household & Beauty businesses. Use scan data and case sell-out to build tailored promo calendars that protect and grow shelf space for your top brands. Include trade-funded promotions, end-aisle features, and themed events (e.g., family value weeks) and tie them to strict post-promo ROI analysis.
reasoning: Grocery delivers €20.42M revenue and ~68% of total revenue, with €5.60M gross profit and ~31% margin, making it the primary growth and profit engine. Dunnes, Musgrave, and Tesco together account for ~67% of total revenue (~€18.25M), so even a small uplift here has outsized impact. A 4.3% uplift on total revenue (€27.8M) is realistic and conservative versus the past DTC campaign’s 36.8% uplift expectation, because this focuses on large, mature customers where incremental growth tends to be single digits. The budget (~1.3% of Grocery revenue over the period) covers trade funding, in-store activation, and shopper marketing. JBPs are a proven way to secure feature and display, defend space, and influence retailer marketing calendars; aligning with their promo windows should drive incremental cases across Food and Household & Beauty while maintaining margin through disciplined promo depth and mix control.
channels: Retailer Media (Tesco Media, Dunnes/Musgrave retail media)

title: Scale High-Margin Online & DTC Using Learnings from Past Performance Marketing Campaign
description: Expand the existing DTC and Online program that previously targeted a €275k revenue impact with 36.8% uplift by increasing media efficiency and layering in retention mechanics. Focus on your most profitable brands (e.g., Kinetica and Green Aware with strong gross profit per € revenue) and bundles that mirror Grocery bestsellers. Implement performance campaigns around high-intent searches and social interest (Google Shopping, Meta) and add a structured email and SMS lifecycle (welcome, abandon cart, replenishment reminders) plus a simple tiered loyalty program that rewards repeat purchases.
reasoning: Online currently delivers €0.75M revenue and €0.40M gross profit (~53% margin), making it your highest-margin scaled channel and a strong candidate for incremental investment. The prior DTC campaign targeted €275k incremental revenue on a €120k budget (≈2.3x ROAS on incremental revenue). Assuming similar or slightly improved efficiency by applying learnings (better audience targeting, creative testing, and more robust lifecycle flows), increasing the budget by 50% to €180k and adding retention triggers can reasonably target ~€450k incremental revenue over 6 months (≈2.5x incremental revenue per € spent). This equates to ~60% growth versus current Online revenue, but only ~1.6% uplift on total company revenue, which is achievable without stressing operations. Focusing on higher-margin brands improves profit leverage, while loyalty and lifecycle flows protect CAC by driving repeat orders.

title: Accelerate Kinetica & Green Aware Penetration via Convenience and Wholesale Activation
description: Run a combined brand-channel push to grow distribution and rate of sale for Kinetica and Green Aware within Convenience and Wholesale. Prioritize incremental listings, eye-level facings, and counter-top or front-of-store displays, supported by sampling, on-pack incentives (e.g., multibuy, price-marked packs where appropriate), and geo-targeted digital ads directing to nearby stockists. Negotiate with BWG and other wholesale-driven groups for tactical displays and menu placements where relevant (e.g., gyms, cafés).
reasoning: Kinetica (€1.61M revenue, €0.63M gross profit, ~39% margin) and Green Aware (€0.84M revenue, €0.27M gross profit, ~33% margin) are high-potential businesses with solid profitability that can benefit from impulse and top-up channels. Convenience and Wholesale together deliver ~€5.30M revenue and €1.86M gross profit; a targeted uplift of ~12% within these channels (~€650k incremental revenue) is reasonable if listings, visibility, and activation materially improve. BWG alone contributes €1.87M revenue and €0.69M gross profit; a 10–15% uplift from BWG via enhanced presence and promotions would cover a large share of the target. The budget funds listing fees, POS, sampling, and geo-targeted ads. Convenience shoppers are highly responsive to in-store visibility and simple price prompts, and using Wholesale to seed more outlets increases physical availability, a key driver of volume growth.

title: Launch a Value-Focused Multi-Brand Retention Program for Top 5 Retail Customers
description: Develop a customer value program aimed at Dunnes, Musgrave, Tesco, UK, and BWG that rewards them for joint initiatives and volume commitments across Food and Household & Beauty. Offer structured incentives tied to volume tiers, NPD launches, and compliance to agreed in-store standards (planogram adherence, display execution). Include quarterly business reviews (QBRs) for each key account with data dashboards on performance, margin, and promo effectiveness, and co-developed activation plans.
reasoning: The top 5 customers generate ~€22.66M revenue (~81% of total) and ~€6.24M gross profit, so even modest incremental growth and churn prevention have a large effect. A 3–4% incremental uplift limited to these customers equates to ~€700–€900k incremental revenue; targeting €800k (~2.9% at total-company level) is realistic. The budget covers incremental trade terms, business review support, and data/BI tools. Given the year-on-year decline between 2023 and 2024 (revenue down by ~45% and units down by ~45%), stabilizing and then growing these core accounts is critical. Focusing on joint value (volume + margin) rather than aggressive discounting protects profit. QBRs and data transparency help retailers see the benefit of supporting your brands versus competitors and provide an early-warning system for space or share losses.

title: Rebuild Volume and Frequency with a Cross-Channel 'Everyday Value Essentials' Campaign
description: Create an umbrella value platform across Food and Household & Beauty (e.g., ‘Everyday Value Essentials’) featuring key SKUs that drive high units and household penetration. Run consistent price-point communication and bundle offers across Grocery, Convenience, and Online, combined with recipe/content marketing and household tips to increase basket size. Align with retailers’ own value messaging to secure placement in their leaflets, apps, and online banners. Mirror the offer on your DTC site and use email to push multi-pack and subscribe-and-save options.
reasoning: Year-on-year, units dropped from 904k (2023) to 497k (2024), a ~45% decline, which suggests either distribution losses, price sensitivity, or reduced purchase frequency. A consistent value campaign focused on essential, high-velocity SKUs can help regain lost volume without eroding brand equity, especially if executed as structured value (bundles, multi-buys) rather than blunt discounts. Targeting a ~6% uplift on Food and Household & Beauty combined (together ~€23.8M revenue) would generate ~€1.4M incremental revenue; taking a conservative portion (~€0.9M, 3.2% at total level) as attributable to this 6-month initiative is reasonable. The budget funds creative development, retailer media, POS, and coordinated digital comms. Cross-channel consistency ensures shoppers see the same value message whether in-store or online, increasing both awareness and basket-building opportunities.

title: Grow International and UK Business with Focused Key Account & Digital-Lead Expansion
description: Implement a structured export growth program centered on the UK and existing International channel customers. Prioritize deepening penetration in current accounts (e.g., UK customer segment worth ~€2.15M revenue) by expanding ranges of Food, Kinetica, and Green Aware. Support this with market-specific digital campaigns (UK-targeted social and search), working in tandem with local distributors and retailers. Develop English-market hero SKUs and test them via online marketplaces and DTC shipping where operationally viable.
reasoning: International and UK combined currently account for ~€3.35M revenue (International €1.19M, UK customer €2.15M) with solid absolute gross profit. A targeted 20% uplift across these segments over 6 months would yield ~€0.67M incremental revenue; setting a goal of €0.7M (~2.5% of total revenue) is aggressive but plausible if new listings and digital demand generation succeed. The budget allows for trade marketing with distributors, UK/International digital advertising, and limited marketplace tests. Diversifying growth into International reduces dependence on domestic Grocery while leveraging existing brand equity and ranges. Digital-led demand can help convince overseas retailers to expand listings by demonstrating consumer interest and online sell-through.
